proposal:
Hi there,

A premium single-product Shopify Advanced store with tracking gaps across Shop Pay paths, an LCP in the 6–45s range on mobile, and 35% in-app browser traffic is a very specific kind of problem — and the fact that you've already chased down Slick double-init and the cart drawer Accept header tells me you want a peer, not a tutorial. I'll keep this direct.

A close reference is rypgolf.com, where I rebuilt the PDP and section structure to bring mobile LCP under 2.5s on a heavy product page, and zenduradental.com, where I handled server-side event work via a custom Node app feeding Shopify and external systems. For tracking specifically, I've shipped sGTM + Stape setups with GA4, Meta CAPI, and Clarity firing consistently across cart-led and Shop Pay / dynamic checkout flows.

On tracking integrity — the AddToCart vs Begin Checkout gap is almost always Shop Pay and dynamic checkout buttons skipping the cart entirely, so the cart-page-based AddToCart listener never fires. I'd move you to server-side via GTM web + Stape (or your existing sGTM if you have one), and fire AddToCart from the product form submit and the /cart/add.js fetch interception, not the cart page load. Begin Checkout fires on the checkout button click and on Shop Pay click. Purchase fires server-side from the Shopify order webhook through Stape, which fixes the once-a-week Clarity Purchase problem — that's Clarity dropping the session at the checkout.shopify.com handoff, so client-side Purchase is unreliable by design on Advanced. GA4, Meta Pixel + CAPI, and Clarity all get the same event payload with consistent event IDs for dedup.

On PDP performance — a 6.8s LCP on Clarity and 45s on PageSpeed mobile usually means the LCP element (likely the hero product image) is being rendered after a chain of render-blocking JS, plus an oversized payload. I'd preload the LCP image with correct srcset and fetchpriority, defer or async all non-critical scripts, strip unused JS from apps that don't need to load on PDP (Affirm, reviews, anything not above the fold), inline only critical CSS, and lazy-load the rest. Target LCP under 2.5s and Performance 70+ on mobile is realistic on a single-product PDP once the script load order is fixed.

The webkit.messagehandlers errors are iOS in-app trying to call native bridge methods that don't exist outside the host app — those go away once you route users out. I'll add UA detection on landing, a soft prompt with the external-browser handoff, and keep the in-app path functional as a fallback.

Source maps I'll enable in your build so the 57% generic script errors become readable. The button overlap on the PDP review submit I'll repro on a clean session and patch the CSS/z-index conflict. Console error sweep I'll do at the end as a clean pass.

On the preview theme QA — happy to do a delta analysis: what's improved, what regressed, what's net-new broken, with screenshots and a short Loom so you can decide go/no-go before publishing.

Hi there,

A premium single-product Shopify Advanced store with daily sales, 80% mobile traffic, and 35% in-app browser sessions has a very specific failure surface, and the fact that you've already chased down Slick double-init and the cart drawer Accept header tells me you want a peer, not a tutorial. I'll keep this direct.

A close reference is rypgolf.com, where I rebuilt PDP performance on Shopify 2.0, killed render-blocking and unused JS, and got mobile LCP and Lighthouse into healthy territory. For server-side tracking and custom event work, zenduradental.com is the better reference, that's a Node.js + React Shopify app handling real-time API calls and event integrity end to end.

On tracking, the Purchase undercount and the AddToCart vs Begin Checkout gap both point at the same root cause: Shop Pay and dynamic checkout buttons skip the cart, and client-side pixels lose users the moment checkout moves to checkout.shopify.com. I'd move GA4 and Meta to server-side via GTM + Stape, fire Purchase from the Shopify order webhook (deduped with event_id), and add a Begin Checkout trigger on Shop Pay and dynamic button clicks before the redirect. Clarity stays client-side but gets a custom Purchase event sent from the thank-you page and the Order Status script so it stops losing the conversion.

For PDP performance, with LCP at 6.8s on Clarity and 45s on PageSpeed mobile, the LCP element and the hero image pipeline are where I'd start. Defer or inline-critical Slick and any third-party JS, preload the hero with correct fetchpriority and a properly sized srcset, split the app blocks that are blocking main thread, and audit Affirm, Klaviyo, and review apps for async loading. 70+ Lighthouse and sub-2.5s LCP on mobile is realistic once the render-blocking and main-thread tasks are cleared.

On the FB/IG in-app browser question, my recommendation is detection plus a soft "Open in Safari/Chrome" handoff rather than hardening the in-app checkout. The webkit.messagehandlers errors and Shop Pay friction inside the in-app webview aren't fully fixable, you're fighting Apple Pay and passkeys that don't exist in that context. A dismissible banner on PDP and cart with a deep link out converts better than trying to patch the webview.

Smaller items: Affirm duplicate publicKey is usually a script included twice via app embed and theme.liquid, easy fix once I see the source. I'll enable source maps in the build so the 57% generic script errors become readable, sweep the console, and repro the review submit button overlap with a clean fix.

For the preview theme, I'll run a delta against live: tracking events, LCP, console errors, network waterfall, and any net-new regressions, delivered as a short Loom plus a written checklist before you publish.

Hourly works for me, I'd rather bill what it actually takes than pad. Phase 1 (server-side tracking, Affirm dupe, source maps, review button, console sweep) is realistic in 24 to 48 hours from kickoff. Phase 2 (PDP performance + in-app browser handoff) lands inside the same week. Let's connect over a quick Zoom or chat and I can start on Phase 1 today.
